title: The Verb — Form I Past Verb (Al-Fiʿl al-Māḍī)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 12; Ryding Ch. 21–22)
objectives: Conjugate regular Form I triliteral verbs in the past tense (al-māḍī) using subject suffixes.
Distinguish the three Form I stem vowel classes (فَعَلَ, فَعِلَ, فَعُلَ).
Apply V-S-O word order and the singular-verb agreement rule before overt plural subjects.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 6: What are the three schematic letters used to represent a triliteral root?

sections.heading: The Form I Past Verb & Stem Vowels
sections.body: Arabic dictionaries cite verbs in the 3rd-person masculine singular past tense (e.g., كَتَبَ 'he wrote'). Depending on the verb, the middle radical takes fatḥah (فَعَلَ — usually active/transitive, like كَتَبَ), kasrah (فَعِلَ — often temporary states/perception, like عَلِمَ 'to know'), or ḍammah (فَعُلَ — always intransitive permanent traits, like كَرُمَ 'to be noble').

sections.label: Verbal Sentence Agreement (V-S-O)
sections.summary: In a classical verbal sentence (Verb + Subject + Object), when the verb precedes an overt plural noun subject, the verb remains SINGULAR and agrees with the subject only in gender (masculine or feminine).

sections.heading: Selected Form I Past Conjugation (كَتَبَ — to write)

sections.irab: كَتَبَ: فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى الفَتْحِ | الطُّلَّابُ: فَاعِلٌ مَرْفُوعٌ بِالضَّمَّةِ | الدَّرْسَ: مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ مَنْصُوبٌ بِالفَتْحَةِ
sections.notes: Even though الطُّلَّابُ is plural, the preceding verb كَتَبَ stays masculine singular (never كَتَبُوا الطُّلَّابُ).

sections.heading: Silent Alif al-Fāriqah
sections.body: The 3rd-person masculine plural suffix ـُوا (e.g., كَتَبُوا) ends in a silent alif (alif al-fāriqah) that distinguishes plural verbs from nouns ending in wāw.
